items.title: Drones set Russian cargo ship on fire in Gulf of Finland
items.why: Russian officials say two drones hit the Kaliningrad-bound cargo ship Sparta II in international waters on Saturday morning. The burning ship drifted into Finnish waters; Finland says other shipping is not at risk. No one has claimed the attack, and no injuries were reported.
items.matters: Finland told its NATO allies and briefly restricted air and sea traffic in the eastern gulf.

items.title: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, South Africa's first woman deputy president, dies at 71
items.why: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka died on Friday evening of complications from a medical procedure about two weeks earlier, her family said. She was South Africa's deputy president from 2005 to 2008 and led UN Women from 2013 to 2021.
items.matters: President Cyril Ramaphosa and UN chief António Guterres led tributes to a long-time campaigner for women's rights.

items.title: Verstappen inherits Las Vegas pole after Antonelli engine penalty
items.why: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, the new world champion, set the fastest time in Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying, 0.258 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen. A five-place grid penalty for an extra engine part drops Antonelli to sixth, so Verstappen starts on pole beside George Russell.
items.matters: The race starts on Saturday at 20:00 local time in Las Vegas, early Sunday in Europe.

items.title: Cricket Australia gives Pat Cummins unanimous backing as Test captain
items.why: Cricket Australia's board says Pat Cummins keeps its 'unanimous support' as captain, after former teammates Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft said the 2018 ball-tampering plot was widely known. Cummins denies knowing. The board ruled out a new inquiry but set up a forum for players to share accounts.
items.matters: Separately, Fox Cricket says Khawaja and David Warner will be 'rested' from its commentary for the coming weeks.

items.title: Magnitude 6.7 earthquake shakes central Peru; no injuries reported
items.why: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck central Peru's Junín region on Friday evening, about 129km deep, Peru's Geophysical Institute says. Civil defence officials reported landslides on roads, damaged homes and a hospital, and power cuts, but no injuries. Shaking was felt in the capital, Lima.
items.matters: Peru sits on one of the world's most active earthquake zones; deep quakes like this can be felt hundreds of kilometres away.

items.title: US media report hacks at FBI crime database and farm agency
items.why: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center, used by police across the US, NBC News and CNN reported on Friday. Separately, a US Department of Agriculture system for paying farmers was hit by a cyberattack, officials said. It is unclear who is responsible.
items.matters: The FBI database holds warrant and background-check records used by police every day.

items.title: US jury convicts man of starting deadly 2025 Palisades Fire
items.why: A federal jury in Los Angeles convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of starting the blaze that became the January 2025 Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people. His first trial ended without a verdict in June. He faces five to 40 years in prison, prosecutors say.
items.matters: The fire destroyed more than 6,800 buildings in Los Angeles and Malibu, Cal Fire says.

items.title: Bolivian university holds guinea pig festival with races and fashion show
items.why: Students at the Public University of El Alto, next to Bolivia's seat of government La Paz, held their second guinea pig festival on Friday. Guinea pigs raced, boxed, were weighed and paraded in costumes; the heaviest weighed 2.5 kilograms. A symbolic guinea pig wedding closed the event.
items.matters: Organisers want to revive the Andean animal, domesticated there thousands of years ago, in Bolivian diets and rituals.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches after 13-year wait to record sales
items.why: Rockstar Games says the video game took about $3.79bn in retail sales in its first day after going on sale on Thursday, nearly five times Grand Theft Auto V's first day in 2013. Reviews have been glowing: its Metacritic score is 99 out of 100.
items.matters: Rockstar calls it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history; the game cost more than $1bn to make.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 for first time since July
items.why: The cryptocurrency bitcoin dropped below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, Reuters reported, as a sell-off in AI-linked shares spread to riskier assets. Bloomberg put it 5.1% lower at about $58,333 late on Friday.

items.title: Nvidia shares tumble after report of US regulator accounting inquiry
items.why: Shares in US chipmaker Nvidia fell about 14% on Friday, CNBC reports, after Reuters said Securities and Exchange Commission staff were examining possible accounting issues. The SEC declined to comment; an inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. Nvidia has had seven straight weekly losses.
items.matters: Nvidia's chips power much of the AI industry, so its troubles affect the wider stock market.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims proof of Riemann hypothesis using Claude AI
items.why: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic, said on Friday that, working with its Claude model, he had found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a problem about prime numbers open since 1859. He released it only in Lean, a language computers use to check proofs.
items.matters: It is a $1m Millennium Prize problem; mathematicians say checking the proof and explaining it to humans will take time.

items.title: US court jails Indian man over plot to kill Sikh separatist
items.why: A federal judge in New York sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months, more than 19 years, on Friday for plotting to have Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun killed. US prosecutors say an Indian intelligence officer directed the plot; India denies any involvement.
items.matters: The case has strained relations between the United States and India, and between India and Canada.

items.title: Estonia to close all road crossings with Russia from 1 December
items.why: Estonia's government decided on Friday to shut its five road checkpoints with Russia for six months from 1 December, citing hostile Russian activity; rail freight will continue. Russia's foreign ministry accused Estonia of trying to "erect a new Iron Curtain".
items.matters: About 760,000 crossings were made this year; Finland has kept its border with Russia closed since 2023.

items.title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper
items.why: Denmark ordered Russia's defence attaché to leave within seven days on Friday. Its intelligence service says Russian intelligence planned to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner at a September concert near Copenhagen; two Danish men are charged. Russia's embassy called the move "vengeful" and says no evidence was shown.
items.matters: Danish intelligence says it is the first Russian assassination attempt of its kind in Denmark.

items.title: EU and UK agree post-Brexit reset on youth mobility and trade
items.why: At a summit in Brussels on Friday, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and EU leaders agreed a youth scheme letting up to 100,000 young people from each side live and work in the other for up to three years, plus deals on food standards and linking carbon markets.
items.matters: EU officials say the deal depends on Britain agreeing lower university fees for EU students within six months.

items.title: 57th International Film Festival of India opens in Goa
items.why: The 57th International Film Festival of India opened on Friday in Panaji, Goa, and runs until 28 November. It is showing 159 international films from 86 countries, chosen from about 1,400 entries, opening with Polish director Paweł Pawlikowski's Cannes prize-winner Fatherland.
items.matters: Its theme is 'Stories Without Borders', with Russia as partner country and Spain as country of honour.

items.title: Poland says Russian missiles crashed on its soil near European drills
items.why: Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone fell on its territory on Friday during an attack on Ukraine; a Kh-101 cruise missile came down near Nowy Lipowiec, about 60km from the Ukrainian border. Nobody was hurt. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it a likely intentional provocation.
items.matters: The objects fell near drills by European troops preparing a possible Ukraine mission; NATO chief Mark Rutte visits Warsaw on Saturday.
items.changed: Updated: officials say two missiles and a drone fell near European troop drills; NATO's chief visits Warsaw on Saturday

items.title: Spain to face France in Nations League quarter-finals
items.why: Friday's draw in Nyon, Switzerland, also paired England with Norway, Portugal with the Netherlands and Belgium with Germany. The two-legged ties will be played between 25 and 30 March, and the finals tournament on 9 to 13 June, at a venue not yet chosen.

items.title: Myanmar rejects UN court ruling that it committed genocide against Rohingya
items.why: Myanmar's military government on Friday called "unfair" the International Court of Justice's ruling that its forces committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims in 2017. The court, in The Hague, ordered compensation and safe return for those displaced; it was the first time it found a state responsible for genocide.
items.matters: About 1.2 million Rohingya live in camps in Bangladesh; the court has very limited means of enforcing its rulings.

items.title: Iraqi forces enter Kataib Hezbollah stronghold after oil smuggling dispute
items.why: Iraqi troops and police deployed on Friday in Jurf al-Sakhar, in Babil province south of Baghdad, under a deal for the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah to leave. The government accuses the group of smuggling state oil worth hundreds of millions of dollars; it denies this.
items.matters: The US has pressed Iraq to disarm Iran-aligned militias, some of which have attacked US forces this year.

items.title: Young people protest over living costs in more than 25 European countries
items.why: Students and workers rallied across Europe on Friday: in Italy the CGIL union held a general strike with protests in more than 100 places, and there were marches in Germany, Austria, Croatia, Spain and Britain. They want better wages, cheaper housing and more spending on education rather than defence.
items.matters: Police in Vienna used pepper spray and made arrests; more protests are planned this weekend, including in France.

items.title: Storm kills at least three, damages thousands of homes in southern Brazil
items.why: A storm with gusts of up to 114 km/h hit the town of Tupanciretã, in Rio Grande do Sul state, early on Friday. City officials say three people died. Officials estimate that most of the town's roughly 8,600 homes were damaged, thousands of them losing their roofs.
items.matters: The state released 2 million reais in emergency funds and President Lula sent federal emergency teams.

sources.name: Rio Grande do Sul state government

items.title: Russian barrage damages three Kyiv bridges; at least nine killed in Ukraine
items.why: Russian missiles and drones hit three bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv overnight into Friday. Kyiv's mayor says seven people died in the capital and 17 were injured; Ukrainian officials put the national toll at at least nine. Russia says it targeted bridges used for military supplies.
items.matters: France has asked for an urgent UN Security Council meeting; as of Saturday morning no date had been announced.
items.changed: Updated: officials say at least nine were killed, seven in Kyiv; no date yet for a UN Security Council meeting

items.title: El Salvador's Bukele registers to run for a third term
items.why: President Nayib Bukele registered with El Salvador's electoral tribunal on Thursday night to seek a third consecutive term in the election on 28 February 2027. A 2025 constitutional change by his party scrapped term limits and run-off votes and lengthened terms to six years.
items.matters: Polls suggest he will win; critics say he has built a de facto one-party state, which he denies.

items.title: Guinea declares end of its mpox outbreak after 42 days without cases
items.why: Guinea's health minister, Khaïté Sall, declared the West African country's mpox outbreak over, effective 17 November, after two incubation periods with no new cases. The outbreak began in September 2024 in Macenta, in the south-east; Guinee360 reports 2,395 confirmed cases and six deaths.
items.matters: Guinea vaccinated 17,660 people during the response, which was supported by WHO and UNICEF.

items.title: Anthropic shares slide on second day as AI sell-off spreads
items.why: Anthropic's shares closed 8.5% lower at $88.91 in New York on Friday, their second day of trading, still above their $83 listing price, CNBC and CNN report. US tech stocks fell again. Earlier, Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi each closed more than 5% lower.
items.matters: The S&P 500 is more than 10% below its October record, a fall markets call a correction, ABC reports.
items.changed: Updated: Friday closing price added; Anthropic's shares ended the day down 8.5%
Updated: officials say no deaths or major damage were reported
items.title: Cyclone Akvan hits Odisha coast; officials report no deaths so far
items.why: Akvan crossed the coast near Gopalpur in India's Odisha state on Friday morning with winds of 70 to 90 km/h, India's weather department says. Odisha officials say about 370,000 people were evacuated and no deaths or major damage have been reported so far.
items.matters: Heavy rain continues in south Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh; more than 65 trains were cancelled.

items.title: Japan's core inflation rises to 2.2% in October, above central bank target
items.why: Consumer prices in Japan excluding fresh food rose 2.2% in the year to October, up from 2.1% in September but just below the 2.3% economists expected, government data showed on Friday. Headline inflation rose to 2.3% after household energy subsidies ended in September.
items.matters: Many investors expect the Bank of Japan to raise its 1.25% interest rate in December, making borrowing dearer.

items.title: Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo, dies after swallowing a visitor's hat
items.why: Cincinnati Zoo, in the US state of Ohio, said on Thursday that Fiona, its nine-year-old Nile hippo, had died. A knitted hat thrown by a visitor was blown into her enclosure by a ceiling fan; vets spent about 11 days trying to help her pass it.
items.matters: Born six weeks early in 2017, she became an internet sensation as people around the world followed her fight to survive.

items.title: Ben Shelton reaches ATP Finals semi-finals for the first time
items.why: American Ben Shelton reached his first ATP Finals semi-final in Turin, Italy. On Saturday he plays Carlos Alcaraz, who won all three group matches without dropping a set; top seed Alexander Zverev meets Daniil Medvedev, who beat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4 on Friday.
items.matters: He is the youngest American to reach the last four since Andy Roddick in 2004, the ATP says.
items.changed: Updated: Shelton will face Carlos Alcaraz in Saturday's first semi-final; Zverev plays Medvedev in the evening.

items.title: House panel says US approved over 879,000 AI chips for China
items.why: The US House Foreign Affairs Committee released licence records on Thursday showing the Commerce Department approved more than 879,000 of 3.4 million requested Nvidia H200 and AMD chips for Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026. Buyers included Tencent and Alibaba.
items.matters: It is unclear how many licences led to shipments; Nvidia says it has since stopped sending H200 chips to China.

items.title: Somalia expels UAE ambassador, accusing Abu Dhabi of interference
items.why: Somalia's government gave the United Arab Emirates' ambassador 72 hours to leave on Thursday and recalled its own envoy, accusing the UAE of "blatant aggression" and of backing regional states that oppose the federal government. The UAE called the move escalatory and hostile.
items.matters: The UAE runs ports at Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo, in regions where Somalia's federal government has little control.

items.title: Haiti police say raid killed at least 34 suspected gang members
items.why: Haiti's national police say an operation on Thursday in Martissant, a gang-held district of the capital, Port-au-Prince, killed at least 34 suspected gang members, with no officers or civilians hurt. It involved a government task force supported by a private firm founded by Erik Prince.
items.matters: The UN says more than 2,250 people were killed in security operations in Haiti in the first nine months of 2026.

items.title: Kushner says Russia 'comfortable' with NATO-style guarantees for Ukraine
items.why: US envoy Jared Kushner said during a "Coalition of the Willing" meeting of more than 25 leaders in the German capital, Berlin, on Thursday that Russia is comfortable with post-war guarantees for Ukraine based on NATO's Article 5. Russia has not commented. Trump joined by phone after meeting Putin.
items.matters: Zelensky wants Europe in US-led talks with Russia; France's Macron urged allies to "reopen the question" of Ukraine joining NATO.

items.title: Brazil recognises Indigenous land of Amazon chief Raoni
items.why: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visited 94-year-old Kayapó leader Raoni Metuktire in Mato Grosso state on Thursday as Brazil declared the 362,000-hectare Kapôt Nhinore territory the permanent possession of the Mẽbêngôkre and Yudjá peoples. The Indigenous peoples minister says about 84% of it is forest.
items.matters: It is a step towards full legal protection; more than 200 farms overlap the land, and rural producers oppose it.

items.title: US sells first deep-sea mining leases off American Samoa despite court ruling
items.why: The US Interior Department auctioned two areas covering about 31 million acres (12.5 million hectares) of Pacific seabed off American Samoa on Thursday, for $6m in total. A federal judge ruled on Monday that a US fisheries agency broke endangered species law in approving the sale.
items.matters: Miners want nodules rich in nickel and cobalt for batteries; conservation groups say mining could harm whales, turtles and corals.

sources.name: US Bureau of Ocean Energy Management

items.title: Blackpool sack head coach hours after wishing him happy birthday
items.why: English third-tier club Blackpool wished head coach Ian Evatt a happy 45th birthday on social media at 9:08am on Thursday, then announced his departure at 4pm. The team is 20th of 24 in League One after one win in its last 10 league games.

items.title: UK tribunal rules government must confirm secret encryption order to Apple
items.why: Britain's Investigatory Powers Tribunal ruled on Thursday that the Home Office must confirm it issued Apple a secret notice seeking access to encrypted user data. It rejected the government's claim that confirming this would harm national security, calling that "fanciful".
items.matters: Apple withdrew its strongest iCloud encryption option for UK users in 2025 over the dispute; a fuller hearing is due in 2027.

items.title: Russian drone attack on Kyiv kills one and damages two embassies
items.why: Russian drones struck Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, on Thursday, killing a 26-year-old man and injuring at least four people, Ukrainian officials say. The Dutch and Austrian embassies were damaged and windows broke at St Volodymyr's Cathedral; embassy staff were unhurt.
items.matters: Russia's embassy in the Netherlands says it was "not a targeted attack".

items.title: Saudi-led coalition says it shot down Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh
items.why: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh early on Saturday; AFP and Reuters journalists in the city reported explosions. It followed coalition strikes on Friday on the port of Hodeidah and sites in Sanaa. No casualties were reported.
items.matters: Houthi forces are also pressing towards Aden, the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government.
items.changed: Updated: the coalition says it intercepted three more missiles fired at Riyadh early on Saturday
Updated: talks continued into Saturday; the presidency says a deal is close but not yet agreed
items.title: COP31 climate talks run into overtime amid row over fossil fuels
items.why: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ran past Friday's deadline. Negotiators worked overnight on a new draft that drops all mention of fossil fuels and a $120bn adaptation goal. The EU, Panama, Ghana and others want a clear move away from fossil fuels; Saudi Arabia and other producers object.
items.matters: COP31 president Murat Kurum said on Saturday: "We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet."
